text: In a certain camera, a combination of four similar thin convex lenses is arranged axially in contact. Then the power of the combination and the total magnification in comparison to the power(p) and magnification (m) for each lens will be, respectively
explanation: In a camera with a series combination of four similar thin convex lenses, the effective power and total magnification of this combination can be calculated as follows:Effective Power: When lenses are in contact, their powers add up. Therefore, the effective power peff of the combination is the sum of the powers of each individual lens: peff = p1 + p2 + p3 + p4 = 4pTotal Magnification: The total magnification meff is the product of the magnifications of each lens in the series: meff = m1 × m2 × m3 × m4 = m4Thus, for a combination of four identical lenses, the effective power is four times the power of a single lens, and the effective magnification is the fourth power of the magnification of a single lens.

text: Given below are two statements: [2024] Statement I: Image formation needs regular reflection and/or refraction. Statement II: The variety in colour of objects we see around us is due to the constituent colours of the light incident on them

options.A: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
options.B: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
options.C: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
options.D: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.

explanation: Statement I: Image formation needs regular reflection and/or refraction.This statement is correct. Image formation in mirrors and lenses occurs through regular (specular) reflection and refraction. For example, in mirrors, light reflects off the surface in a regular manner to form an image, and in lenses, light bends (refracts) as it passes through the lens material to form an image.Statement II: The variety in colour of objects we see around us is due to the constituent colours of the light incident on them.This statement is also correct. The color of an object we perceive depends on the wavelengths of light it reflects. For example, a red object reflects primarily red wavelengths, and we see that color. The variety in the colors of objects is due to the combination of the different wavelengths of light that are incident on them.Conclusion: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.Final Answer: (c) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
